text.approach: Identical to Rebel Yell. Drive SR 20 to Washington Pass, then about 4 miles east to a wide pullout on the south side of the highway near milepost 166, at roughly 4,250 ft (about 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake road, about 2 miles east of the hairpin turn). No Northwest Forest Pass is required on the highway shoulder. Descend a steep, faint scree path about 300 ft to Early Winters Creek, cross on logs, then follow the climbers' trail steeply uphill to a wooded bench at 6,400-6,600 ft - the standard low camp, with a year-round spring about 200 yards north of the trail and a seasonal spring in the sandy gully above. Above the bench the trail fades; follow cairns up loose gullies, trending right and up, into the main gully below Burgundy Col at 7,800-7,950 ft. The gully holds a roughly 40-degree snow finger into midsummer. Roughly 3.5 miles and about 3,700 ft of gain to the col in 3-4 hours. From the col, descend 200-300 ft on the south side and traverse right beneath Burgundy Spire's east face on year-round snow with seasonal rock bands until Chianti's east face is in view. Rebel Yell's dihedral is the obvious feature on the right side of the face; Lichen Bouquet's ramp starts directly below the summit and leans left. Under an hour from the col.

text.overview: The original 1952 first-ascent line up Chianti Spire, gained by rappelling into the Burgundy-Chianti notch and climbing the peak's north side on then-loose rock; now rarely repeated in favor of the East Face/Rebel Yell.
text.descent: Downclimb or make a short rappel off the summit block back onto the north face, then reverse the line to the Burgundy-Chianti notch. From the notch, traverse north on snow beneath Burgundy Spire's east face and climb the 200-300 ft back up to Burgundy Col - this re-ascent is the sting in the tail and is much easier on firm morning snow than on afternoon slush or bare, sandy rock.
